_comment: SF Symbols rendered on macOS 27.2.1 (26B131) by NSImage symbol images -> CoreUI vector glyph layers -> CGContext(PDF) -> pdftocairo -svg. Units are points at pointSize; SVG viewBox = NSImage.size (the symbol image canvas AppKit uses, including the symbol's built-in margins). Rects are [x, y, w, h] in SVG coordinates (y down). baselineY = text baseline inside the viewBox; capHeight = cap height of the matching SF Pro size; glyphRect = where AppKit places the glyph bitmap (2x pixel-snapped). Files: <symbol>.<weight>.svg = monochrome (black template); .hierarchical = layers with opacity 1 / 0.5 / 0.3 (primary/secondary/tertiary); .multicolor = system colours resolved in light (aqua) appearance; .var-N = variable value N/100 (inactive layers at opacity 0.3).

airdrop.note: Control Center AirDrop button. Private symbol (NSImage(systemSymbolName:) returns nil; rendered via +[NSImage imageWithPrivateSystemSymbolName:accessibilityDescription:]). ControlCenter binary references "airdrop"; CoreTypes com.apple.airdrop UTTypeSymbolName = airdrop. | finder: Finder sidebar AirDrop: CoreTypes com.apple.airdrop UTTypeSymbolName = airdrop (private symbol).

appstore.note: Private symbol: the App Store "A" made of three strokes. Same glyph macOS uses for the Applications folder (CoreTypes com.apple.applications-folder UTTypeSymbolName = appstore), i.e. the Apps/Launchpad header glyph the PC drew.

backward.note: Now Playing previous-track button (filled, as the PC drawing).

extras.why: empty outline to draw your own level into

battery.note: Menu bar battery. ControlCenter binary references battery.100percent / battery.25percent. The menu bar draws the charge level; battery.0percent is the empty outline if you fill the level yourself; battery.100percent.bolt is the charging glyph (multicolor = green fill, guess that the menu bar uses it).

bell.note: Only used by the PC for the "Show Notification Center" Spotlight action; filled like the PC drawing. bell (outline) also rendered.

bluetooth.note: Private symbol. ControlCenter binary references "bluetooth"; System Settings uses it too (CoreTypes com.apple.graphic-icon.bluetooth ISSymbolName = bluetooth). | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: bluetooth. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

bolt.note: Spotlight Actions mode / action rows. SpotlightUIInternal references "bolt.fill".

calendar.note: No current use in shell/ found; plain name match.

camera.note: Screenshot actions in Spotlight; outline like the PC drawing. camera.viewfinder is the Screenshot-app style glyph (not rendered).

chevron.down.note: | finder: Toolbar group-by popup / list disclosure; Finder binary references chevron.down.

chevron.right.note: Submenu arrow (shell) and Finder Forward button. chevron.forward is the layout-direction-aware name; its SVG output is byte-identical to chevron.right in left-to-right layout. Finder binary references chevron.forward. | finder: Toolbar Forward. Finder binary references chevron.forward (byte-identical to chevron.right in LTR).

clipboard.note: Spotlight Clipboard mode (Cmd-4). Not verified against the live Spotlight UI.

controlcenter.note: Menu bar Control Center item. Same glyph System Settings uses for the Control Center pane (ControlCenterSettings.appex ISSymbolName = switch.2).

display.note: Control Center Display module / Mission Control action. ControlCenter binary references "display".

doc.note: Spotlight Files mode and file rows. "doc" is a legacy alias of "document" in CoreGlyphs name_aliases.strings; both render byte-identical. Name kept as "doc" because CoreTypes (Finder sidebar Documents) references "doc". | finder: Sidebar Documents: CoreTypes com.apple.documents-folder UTTypeSymbolName = doc (alias of "document", byte-identical).

ellipsis.note: Apps (Launchpad) header more button; plain three dots as the PC drawing. | finder: Toolbar Action menu. Finder binary references ellipsis, ellipsis.circle and ellipsis.circle.fill; the PC drawing (from 27.2 screenshots) is plain dots. ellipsis.circle also rendered.

folder.note: Spotlight folder rows / New Finder Window action; filled like the PC drawing. Spotlight itself shows real file icons for folders. folder (outline) also rendered.

gear.note: No current use in shell/; System Settings uses "gear" for General (GeneralSettings.appex ISSymbolName = gear). | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: general. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

keyboard.note: Outline keyboard; no current use in shell/.

lock.note: Lock Screen action; filled body like the PC drawing.

magnifyingglass.note: Menu bar Spotlight item and search fields. | finder: Toolbar search.

moon.note: Focus / Do Not Disturb (menu bar, Control Center) and Sleep. Filled like the PC drawing; System Settings Focus uses moon.fill.

person.note: No current use in shell/; filled like the PC drawing.

power.note: Restart / Shut Down / Log Out actions.

screen.mirror.note: Control Center Screen Mirroring. macOS uses two overlapping rectangles (ControlCenter binary references rectangle.on.rectangle and rectangle.on.rectangle.slash), not the old AirPlay screen-with-triangle the PC drew.

extras.why: menu bar Sound item, variable value

speaker.note: Control Center Sound slider glyph. ControlCenter binary references speaker.wave.2.fill, speaker.wave.3.fill and speaker.slash.fill. speaker.wave.3.fill is the menu bar Sound item; its .var-0 / .var-20 / .var-50 files are variable values 0, 0.2, 0.5 (0, 1, 2 waves lit; unlit waves at 30 % opacity, as AppKit draws them); the plain file = all lit. Hierarchical files: waves at 50 %; whether a system surface uses hierarchical here is a guess.

square.grid.note: Spotlight Apps mode / Show Apps action; filled squares like the PC drawing. For the Control Center Stage Manager button macOS uses rectangle.3.group (ControlCenter binary reference), rendered as an extra.

sun.note: Control Center Display brightness slider and the light/dark action. Same symbol as System Settings Displays (CoreTypes graphic-icon.display).

terminal.note: New Terminal Window action. apple.terminal is the Terminal-app glyph (Finder references it); "terminal" is a near-identical older glyph, also rendered.

trash.note: Empty Trash action. | finder: Sidebar Trash / Move to Trash; Finder binary references trash.

wifi.note: Menu bar / Control Center Wi-Fi. The menu bar shows signal strength with variable value: .var-0 (nothing lit), .var-20 (dot lit), .var-50 (dot + middle arc lit), plain file = all lit; unlit parts at 30 % opacity, measured from AppKit. All wifi layers are primary, so hierarchical = monochrome (not rendered). | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: wifi. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

xmark.note: Notification close / clear buttons, Quick Look close. | finder: Quick Look close; Finder binary references xmark.

applications.note: Finder sidebar Applications: CoreTypes com.apple.applications-folder UTTypeSymbolName = appstore (private symbol).

arrow.up.down.note: Sort control; Finder binary references arrow.up.arrow.down.

chevron.left.note: Toolbar Back. Finder binary references chevron.backward (byte-identical to chevron.left in LTR).

chevron.small.right.note: Path bar separator and column-view arrow: same chevron.forward glyph drawn at a smaller point size (scale the SVG); no separate "small" symbol exists. chevron.compact.right is a flatter alternative, not rendered.

clock.note: Sidebar Recents: CoreTypes com.apple.finder.recent-items UTTypeSymbolName = clock.

desktop.note: Sidebar Desktop: CoreTypes com.apple.desktop-folder UTTypeSymbolName = menubar.dock.rectangle.

download.note: Sidebar Downloads: CoreTypes com.apple.downloads-folder UTTypeSymbolName = arrow.down.circle.

drive.note: Volumes: CoreTypes com.apple.storage-internal / public.volume UTTypeSymbolName = internaldrive (Macintosh HD, path bar root); com.apple.storage-external and storage-removable use externaldrive (rendered as extra) - pick by volume type.

eject.note: Sidebar eject button; Finder binary references both eject and eject.fill. Filled like the PC drawing; outline also rendered.

eye.note: Quick Look; Finder binary references eye.

group.note: Toolbar Group/Sort By; Finder binary references it.

icloud.note: Sidebar iCloud Drive: CoreTypes com.apple.iCloud UTTypeSymbolName = icloud.

minus.note: Name match; no current use in finder/qml.

network.note: Sidebar Network: CoreTypes com.apple.network-neighborhood UTTypeSymbolName = network. | settings: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: network. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

plus.note: Name match; no current use in finder/qml.

share.note: Toolbar Share; Finder binary references it.

shared.note: Sidebar Shared (shared folders). Finder binary references folder.and.person; the glyph (folder outline with tab line, filled person lower right) matches the PC drawing. folder.badge.person.crop is the older look, not rendered.

tag.note: Toolbar Tags; Finder binary references tag.

view.columns.note: View as Columns; Finder binary references it.

view.gallery.note: View as Gallery; Finder binary references it.

view.icons.note: View as Icons (PC example); Finder binary references it.

view.list.note: View as List; Finder binary references it.

xmark.circle.note: Search field clear button (filled circle with knocked-out X, as the PC drawing); Finder binary references xmark.circle.fill.

network.badge.shield.half.filled.note: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: vpn. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white.

bolt.fill.note: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: energy. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white. Also the Battery pane on Macs without a battery (PowerPreferences.appex representation powersource.battery != YES).

battery.100.note: System Settings sidebar tile symbol for panes: battery. Read from the pane extension Info.plist ISGraphicIconConfiguration or the CoreTypes graphic-icon UTI; the tile draws it monochrome white. battery.100 comes from com.apple.graphic-icon.battery, which PowerPreferences.appex uses when powersource.battery == YES (MacBooks); panes.json says bolt.fill, which is the no-battery (desktop) representation.

skipped.zoom (finder): The two-triangle full-screen glyph is the window zoom/traffic-light artwork drawn by AppKit, not an SF Symbol (no symbol name in CoreGlyphs or CoreGlyphsPrivate matches). Not rendered.
